docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Weclome to NID-24 project. We are building a muscle fatigue tolerant EMG system primary aimed to developing exciting human-computer-interfaces. Our goal is to build a stable pipeline for sEMG signals acquisition. The core pipeline will allow development of diverse applications with ease.

The project is divided into 3 main parts which can studied deeply in the upcoming sections.

  • Hardware: Includes custom ADS1293 based breakout board.
  • Software: Includes development tools.
  • CAD: Includes plans on reducing size of the system to turn this into a wearable and more accessible product.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Modular Software Systems
  • Easy To Get Started No Setup Required
  • Extensive Developer Tools
  • Coin Sized PCBs
  • 100% Open-Source

docs.title: General Architecture
docs.text:
A quick representation of general logic of the system

Electrodes are attached to the human body, ADS1293 receives these analog signals and converts them into digital signals. These digital signals are processed by Teensy 4.0, the board extracts required features and feeds it to the AI model for action mapping. The output is shared to the PC over bluetooth acting like a mouse.

The inital aim of the project is aimed at the application of this system into a non-traditional mouse. However, in the curent phase pointer movement is not supported.

docs.title: Data Reader
docs.text:
The data enters into the application from this point. Data reader manages two internal ring buffers visualisation buffer and main buffer. The main buffer holds 1000 values while visualisation buffer holds 100 data packets.

The visualisation buffer is derived from the main buffer. The buffer holds latest values from the main buffer.

The main buffer is not modified at any stage of processing, each component of the application process it in it's own way without modifying the original buffer.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Analysis Software

Analysis software allows you to observe sEMG signals in real-time. You can create your own datasets using the utility provided. The software is based on modular components allowing you to modify codebase easily. This development pattern allows fault-tolerant system.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Visualise signals in real-time.
  • Create your own datasets.
  • Record observations.
  • Plug and Play software.
  • Modular and fault tolerant architecture.
  • Observe signal features change in real time.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Installation is simple and straightforward follow the steps below to install the application.

  1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/Raghav67816/NID-24.git
  1. Enter into the cloned directory.
cd NID-24/

Info

Please install Python3 before continuing.

  1. Create a virtualenv and install requirements.
pip3 install virtualenv
virtualenv env
source env/bin/activate

pip3 install -r requirements.txt
  1. Run application
sudo ./env/bin/python3 app.py

Info

The application requires to interact with rfcomm utility of Linux system. Thus, root permissions must be provided in the way above.

docs.title: 1. Controller Board cannot connect to PC
docs.text:
The application requires rfcomm utility to enable devices to connect. However, if you have Bluez ≥ 5.4 this will not work because newer version of Bluez have dropped support for rfcomm. However, rfcomm is very stable and completely satisfies the requirements of analysis software.

To fix this, run bluetooth service in compatibility mode

  • Open the bluetooth service file (for systemd)
sudo nano /usr/lib/systemd/system/bluetooth.service
  • Locate the following line
[Service]
Type=dbus
BusName=org.bluez
ExecStart=/usr/libexec/bluetooth/bluetoothd # this one
NotifyAccess=main
#WatchdogSec=10
Restart=on-failure
CapabilityBoundingSet=CAP_NET_ADMIN CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE
LimitNPROC=1
  • Add compatibility flag
[Service]
Type=dbus
BusName=org.bluez
ExecStart=/usr/libexec/bluetooth/bluetoothd --compat  # like this
NotifyAccess=main
#WatchdogSec=10
Restart=on-failure
CapabilityBoundingSet=CAP_NET_ADMIN CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE
LimitNPROC=1
  • Restart bluetooth service and daemon
sudo systemctl restart bluetooth.service
sudo systemctl daemon-reload

docs.title: RFComm Process
docs.text:
RFCommProcess class is responsible for managing the rfcomm process and it's state. It starts the rfcomm process and observes it's state. This class inherits from QProcess and runs the rfcomm process by executing:

sudo rfcomm listen hci0

This also adds an SDP profile internally. When a device connects or disconnects the state is emitted by the class.

docs.title: Signals
docs.text:
com_finished: Emitted when process is finished. The signal returns int exit_code and str message

Info

The class contains a cleanup() function. If you are making your own utilities with rfcomm make sure that you call this function on application exit.

docs.title: EasyEMG Board
docs.text:
EasyEMG board is a custom ADS1293 based breakout board configured for 3-channel / 5 lead application. The design of this board strictly follows the guidelines of datasheet provided by Texas Instruments.

This board is extremely compact a 20x20 mm board looks like a coin sized PCB. This allows us to develop this project into a consumable project.

EasyEMG Board Render. IRL images will shared soon

Features:

  • Super Compact Size (20mm x 20mm)
  • 24-bit ADC resolution
  • Configured for 3 channel / 5 Lead Application
  • Streams data at a frequency of 1 KHz*

The board is being assembled and tested. Actual images will shared soon. For more information about design please refer to Page 63 of the datasheet.

PCB files are available here here

Improvements Pending

The EasyEMG board requires following improvements:

  • Use of correct LDO. (Currently uses a 5v LDO footprint due to human error)
  • Use of JST connectors instead of pin headers.
